en: The Vajraśekhara Yoga Tattvaprajñāpāramitā Sūtra, translated from the Sanskrit original by the Tripitaka Master Vajrabodhi of South India during the Tang Dynasty at Zhongtianzhu (Central India).
Thus have I heard: At one time, the Bhagavān, the Tathāgata of Perfectly Good Accomplishment, was [dwelling] in the Vajra...

Abiding in the wisdom of the equality of all phenomena (*samatājñāna*), you possess various rare and sublime qualities; you have already been able to well protect the precious crown of the supreme Dharma-kingship of all Tathāgatas, transcending the three realms;

you have already been able to well attain the pervasive vajra-wisdom of all Tathāgatas, possessing the sovereign mastery of Mahāyoga that is unimpeded and definitively purifies the wondrous Dharma-wisdom of all Tathāgatas;

you have well and perfectly realized the seal of the ultimate emptiness and quiescence of the equality of all Tathāgatas, such that all activities you undertake are skillfully accomplished, and the various hopes and aspirations of all other sentient beings are able to be fulfilled according to their needs, provided they are blameless.

Having already become well-established in the equality of the three times, the nature of his body, speech, and mind is constant, inexhaustible, vast, and all-pervading; like a vajra, it is immovable and indestructible, equal to that of all Tathāgatas.

The Bhagavān was dwelling in the palace of the King of the Paranirmita-vaśavartin Heaven at the summit of the desire realm—a place where all Tathāgatas constantly reside—and everyone together praised the Great Treasure Treasury Hall.

That palace was constructed of priceless *maṇi* jewels, adorned with an intermingling of various rare and wondrous treasures. The beings within reflected one another, radiating great light. Precious bells and golden tinklets were suspended everywhere; when stirred by a gentle breeze, they produced harmonious and elegant sounds. It was further embellished with variegated canopies, silken banners, floral standards, and colorful whisks, as well as various ornaments such as precious beads, necklaces, and crescent and full-moon shaped decorations—objects cherished by the worthy sages, celestial beings, and immortals.

He was accompanied by eight billion great bodhisattvas, all of whom were fully endowed with the gates of dhāraṇī, the gates of samādhi, and unimpeded, wondrous eloquence; such immeasurable virtues as these could not be fully extolled even if one were to spend many kalpas doing so.
Their names were:

the Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva Vajrapāṇi, the Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva Avalokiteśvara, the Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva Gaganagañja, the Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva Vajramuṣṭi, the Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva Mañjuśrī, the Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva Saccittotpādadharmacakrapravartin, the Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva Ākāśagarbha, and the Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva Sarvamāraparapravādin.

Thus, surrounded before and behind by a multitude of eighty billion great bodhisattvas as their leaders, he proclaimed the True Dharma—good in the beginning, middle, and end; skillful in both words and meaning; pure, complete, and the pristine holy life.
At that time, the World-Honored One, for the sake of the bodhisattvas, expounded the Dharma-gate of the Principle of the Prajñāpāramitā of the Innate Purity of the Self-Nature of All Dharmas.
This gate is precisely the meaning of the term "bodhisattva."
What is called the meaning of the term "bodhisattva"?
It refers to the following:
"The meaning of the term 'supremely wondrous and pure' is the meaning of the term 'bodhisattva';"
The pure meaning of the eternal quiescence of all views is the bodhisattva’s meaning;
the pure meaning of subtle and delightful serenity is the bodhisattva’s meaning;
the pure meaning of the eternal cessation of craving is the bodhisattva’s meaning.
The pure phrase of transcending the womb is the phrase of the bodhisattva;
the pure phrase of the adornment of manifold virtues is the phrase of the bodhisattva;
the pure phrase of the ultimate delight of the mind is the phrase of the bodhisattva.
The phrase "purity of mind" is a phrase for a bodhisattva;
the phrase "purity of form" is a phrase for a bodhisattva;
the phrase "purity of sound" is a phrase for a bodhisattva.
The meaning of the phrase "purity of fragrance" is the phrase for a bodhisattva;
the meaning of the phrase "purity of taste" is the phrase for a bodhisattva;
the meaning of the phrase "purity of touch" is the phrase for a bodhisattva.
Why is this? Because all phenomena are pure by their very nature.
That all phenomena are pure by their very nature is the most supreme purity of the *prajñāpāramitā*.

When the Buddha had thus taught this pure Dharma of the *prajñāpāramitā* principle concerning the meaning of the bodhisattva’s words, he addressed the Bodhisattva Vajrapāṇi and the others, saying: “Bodhisattva Vajrapāṇi!”

If anyone should hear this Dharma-gate of the principle of the *prajñāpāramitā* on the intrinsic purity of all phenomena, and it but once passes through their ears, all afflictive obstructions, karmic actions, and most grievous sins will naturally be extinguished; until they reach enlightenment, they shall not be born in the evil realms.
If one can daily receive, uphold, recite, and contemplate with right mindfulness, one will certainly attain, in this very life, the vajra-samādhi of the equality of all phenomena.
"Having passed through sixteen births as great bodhisattvas, one will certainly attain the nature of the Tathāgata Vajradhara and swiftly realize unsurpassed, perfect enlightenment.
He then uttered the secret mantra: "HŪṂ.

At that time, the World-Honored One again, assuming the form of Vairocana Tathāgata, expounded for the sake of all bodhisattvas the profound principle of the Prajñāpāramitā of the tranquil dharmatā of all Tathāgatas, the gateway to manifesting equal enlightenment.
That is to say:
"The attainment of perfect enlightenment through the equality of the vajra, because the solid nature of great bodhi is like a vajra;
the attainment of perfect enlightenment through the equality of meaning, because great bodhi has the single nature of meaning;"
One attains perfect enlightenment through the equality of phenomena, because the nature of great bodhi is intrinsically pure;
one attains perfect enlightenment through the equality of all karma, because great bodhi is free from all conceptual discrimination.
When the Buddha had thus spoken this gateway of the nature of phenomena (*dharmatā*), he addressed the Bodhisattva Vajrapāṇi, saying: “Vajrapāṇi!

If there are those who hear this gateway to the manifest awakening to the principle of the *prajñāpāramitā* that achieves perfect enlightenment through these four kinds of peaceful natures, and who believe, understand, uphold, recite, and correctly contemplate it with mindfulness, they shall transcend all evil realms and swiftly realize unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment.”
He further spoke these secret words:

"Aṃ. At that time, the Bhagavān, again relying upon the form of Śākyamuni—the one who can subdue all sentient beings difficult to subdue among all Tathāgatas—taught for the sake of the bodhisattvas the Dharma-gate of the Principle of the Prajñāpāramitā of Universal Supreme Equality of All Dharmas.
That is to say:
"The nature of greed is free from conceptual proliferation;
the nature of hatred is free from conceptual proliferation."
Love has the nature of being free from conceptual proliferation (*niṣprapañca*). Why?
Because even all things have the nature of being free from conceptual proliferation.
"The nature of all things being free from conceptual proliferation (*niṣprapañca*) is itself the nature of the Perfection of Wisdom (*prajñāpāramitā*) being free from conceptual proliferation.
Having thus spoken this Dharma of Universal Victory, the Principle of Wisdom for Subduing All Evils, the Buddha addressed Vajrapāṇi Bodhisattva and the others, saying: "Vajrapāṇi!"

If there are those who hear this Dharma gate of the *Prajñāpāramitā* principle of the universal, supreme equality of all phenomena, and who believe, understand, accept, uphold, recite, and correctly contemplate it with mindfulness, even if they were to kill all sentient beings within the three realms, they would never, on account of that, fall into the evil destinies.
Why is this? Because they have already received the discipline of taming the mind;
they will constantly be born in the happy realms, cultivate the practices of enlightenment, and swiftly realize unsurpassed, perfect, and complete awakening.
He further uttered the secret syllable:

“HŪṂ. At that time, the World-Honored One, again relying upon the aspect of the self-nature purity of all Tathāgatas, expounded for the sake of the bodhisattvas the Dharma-gate of the Principle of the Prajñāpāramitā, the Wisdom-Seal of Avalokiteśvara regarding the Equality of All Dharmas.
That is to say:
"The nature of all greed is pure; the nature of all hatred is pure.
Because the nature of all greed is pure, the nature of all defilements is pure, and the nature of all offenses is pure."
Because the nature of all defilements is pure and the nature of sin is pure, the nature of all phenomena is pure and the nature of sentient beings is pure;
because the nature of all phenomena is pure and the nature of sentient beings is pure, the nature of omniscience is pure;
and because the nature of omniscience is pure, the Prajñāpāramitā is supremely pure.
When the Buddha had thus taught this pure Dharma of the Prajñāpāramitā-naya, the Seal of Equal Wisdom, he addressed Vajrapāṇi Bodhisattva and the others, saying: "Vajrapāṇi!"

If there are those who hear this Dharma-gate of the *Prajñāpāramitā-naya* of the Wisdom-Seal of the Sovereign Lord of the Equality of All Dharmas, and who believe, understand, receive, uphold, recite, and correctly contemplate it with mindfulness, then even while amidst the five desires and sensory dusts, they will not be defiled by the faults of adventitious afflictions; just as a lotus flower, though in the mud, is ultimately unstained and unattached, such persons shall swiftly realize unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment.
He further spoke this secret mantra:

“Hrīḥ” (with a long vowel). At that time, the World-Honored One, again relying upon all Tathāgatas as the sign of the triple world, expounded for the sake of the Bodhisattvas the Dharma-gate of the *Prajñāpāramitā-naya* entitled "The Wisdom-Treasury Manifestation of the Empowerment of All Tathāgatas."
That is to say:
"The gift of consecration, because it causes one to attain the rank of a Dharma King over all the three realms;
the gift of wealth and treasures, because it causes all one's aspirations to be fulfilled."
“Pure Dharma-giving is for the purpose of causing one to attain the nature of the jewel of all dharmas;
the giving of food and drink is for the purpose of causing the body, speech, and mind to obtain peace and happiness.
Having thus spoken this treasury of wisdom, the principle of the empowerment of Prajñāpāramitā, the Buddha addressed Vajrapāṇi Bodhisattva and the others, saying:

"If there are those who hear this profound principle of empowerment, the Dharma-gate of the Treasury of Wisdom, and with faith and understanding accept, uphold, read, recite, and correctly contemplate it, they will swiftly fulfill the bodhisattva practices and quickly realize unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment."
He further spoke this secret mantra:

"Taraṃ. At that time, the World-Honored One, relying once more upon the secret treasury of the signs of the eternally abiding wisdom-seal (*jñāna-mudrā*) of all Tathāgatas, proclaimed for the sake of the bodhisattvas the Dharma-gate of the profound *prajñāpāramitā* principle of the Vajra Wisdom-Seal of all Tathāgatas.
That is to say:
"By holding the vajra-body seal of all Tathāgatas, one attains the true nature of all Tathāgatas;
by holding the vajra-speech seal of all Tathāgatas, one attains mastery over all gateways."
By holding the vajra-heart mudrā of all Tathāgatas, one attains the perfection of all samādhis;
by holding the vajra-wielder’s vajra-wisdom mudrā of all Tathāgatas, one attains the supreme body, speech, and mind that are like vajras.
When the Buddha had thus spoken this Dharma-gate of the Seal of Wisdom (*jñāna-mudrā*), he addressed Vajrapāṇi and the others, saying: "Vajrapāṇi!

If there are those who hear this Dharma-gate of the Profound Prajñāpāramitā Principle of the Vajra-Wisdom of All Tathāgatas, and who believe, understand, uphold, recite, and correctly contemplate it with mindfulness, they shall immediately achieve the supreme Vajra-Wisdom Seal. They will attain perfection in all-encompassing wisdom and all manifold activities; their body, speech, and mind-nature will become indestructible like vajra, and they will swiftly realize unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment."
Furthermore, he spoke these secret words:

"Evil. At that time, the World-Honored One, again relying upon the marks of the Tathāgata of all dharmas free from conceptual proliferation, taught for the sake of the bodhisattvas the *Prajñāpāramitā-naya-dharmaparyāya* entitled "The Chapter on the Turning Wheel of Syllables."
That is to say:
"All phenomena are empty because they lack intrinsic nature;
all phenomena are signless because they are free from all signs."
All phenomena are wishless, because they are free from all wishes;
even unto the fact that the intrinsic nature of all phenomena is pure, which is the very purity of the intrinsic nature of the *prajñāpāramitā*.
After the Buddha had thus taught this Dharma of the wheel of syllables of the principle of non-conceptualization (*niṣprapañca-prajñā*), he addressed Vajrapāṇi Bodhisattva and the others, saying:

"If anyone hears this Dharma-gate of the wheel of syllables of the principle of non-conceptualization, and with faith, understanding, and resolve, receives, maintains, recites, and correctly contemplates it, they will attain unimpeded wisdom regarding all phenomena and swiftly realize unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment."
He further spoke these secret words:

"Aṃ (with the vowel *a* pronounced with an upward-sweeping tone and drawn out). At that time, the World-Honored One, again relying upon the sign of all Tathāgatas entering the vast wheel-turning, expounded for the sake of the bodhisattvas the profound principle of the entrance into the vast wheel-turning Prajñāpāramitā, the gateway to the equality of nature.
That is to say:
"By entering the equality of the vajra, one attains entry into the wheel of all Tathāgatas;
by entering the equality of meaning, one attains entry into the wheel of the Dharma of all Bodhisattvas."
They enter the equality of phenomena because they attain entry into the turning of the wheel of the sublime Dharma;
and so on, up to entering the equality of all phenomena, because they attain entry into the equality of all phenomena and attain entry into the turning of the wheel of all dharmas.
When the Buddha had thus taught this entry into the equality of the profound principle of the vast turning wheel of *prajñā*, he addressed Vajrapāṇi Bodhisattva and the others, saying:

"If there are those who hear such a gateway to the equality of the profound principle of the wheel-nature, and who believe, understand, uphold, recite, and correctly contemplate it, they will be well able to awaken to and enter all states of equality, and swiftly realize unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment."
He further uttered the secret syllable:

"HŪṂ. At that time, the World-Honored One, again relying upon the various implements for the vast offerings of all Tathāgatas, proclaimed for the sake of the bodhisattvas the supreme, foremost, and most extensive Dharma-gate of the profound principle of the Prajñāpāramitā concerning the various implements for vast offerings.
That is to say:
"To generate the bodhicitta is itself to perform a vast offering to all Tathāgatas;
to rescue and protect all sentient beings is itself to perform a vast offering to all Tathāgatas."
To abide in the sublime Dharma is itself to perform a vast offering to all Tathāgatas;
likewise, even to write down, uphold, read, recite, maintain right mindfulness, contemplate, and make offerings to the Prajñāpāramitā is itself to perform a vast offering to all Tathāgatas.
When the Buddha had thus spoken this supreme Dharma of the profound principle of the truly pure offering, he addressed Vajrapāṇi and the others, saying:

"If there are those who hear this supreme Dharma-gate of the Prajñā-principle of offering, and who believe, understand, receive, uphold, recite, and correctly contemplate it with right mindfulness, they will swiftly fulfill all the practices of a bodhisattva and quickly realize unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment."
He further uttered the secret mantra:

"Oṃ. At that time, the World-Honored One, relying once more upon the aspect of all Tathāgatas who are able to subdue all sentient beings, proclaimed for the sake of the bodhisattvas the Dharma-gate of the *Prajñāpāramitā-naya*, the Secret Treasury of Wisdom capable of subduing all sentient beings.
That is to say:
"The equality of all sentient beings is the equality of the wrathful;
the subduability of all sentient beings is the subduability of the wrathful."
The true dharmatā of all sentient beings is the true dharmatā of wrath;
the vajra-like nature of all sentient beings is the vajra-like nature of wrath.
"Why is this? Because it tames all sentient beings and causes them to attain bodhi.
Having thus spoken these words on the treasury of wisdom regarding the profound principle of skillful subduing, the Buddha addressed Vajrapāṇi Bodhisattva and the others, saying:

"If there are those who hear this Dharma-gate of the Treasury of Wisdom on the Principle of Subduing, and who believe, understand, uphold, recite, and correctly contemplate it with mindfulness, they will be able to subdue their own faults such as anger; they will also be able to subdue all sentient beings so that they always take birth in the happy realms and experience various sublime joys; in this present life, all enemies will give rise to thoughts of loving-kindness; they will be well able to practice the various bodhisattva deeds and swiftly realize unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment."
Furthermore, he spoke this secret mantra:

"Hao. At that time, the World-Honored One, again relying upon the state of equality in which all Tathāgatas abide, expounded for the sake of the bodhisattvas the Dharma-gate of the Principle of the Profound Prajñāpāramitā, the Supreme Equality of All Dharmas.
That is to say:
"Because all phenomena are the nature of equality, the profound *prajñāpāramitā* is also the nature of equality;
because all phenomena are the nature of the ultimate truth (*paramārtha*), the profound *prajñāpāramitā* is also the nature of the ultimate truth."
Because all phenomena are the very nature of reality (*dharmatā*), the profound *prajñāpāramitā* is also the nature of reality;
even unto the fact that all things possess the nature of functional activity, one should know that the profound *prajñāpāramitā* likewise possesses the nature of functional activity.
When the Buddha had thus spoken this most supreme Dharma of the profound principle of the equality of natures, he addressed the Bodhisattva Vajrapāṇi and the others, saying:

"If there are those who hear this most supreme Dharma-gate of the profound principle of the equality of Prajñāpāramitā, and who believe, understand, receive, uphold, recite, and correctly contemplate it with mindfulness, they will be able to penetrate the profound Prajñāpāramitā of the nature of equal dharmas; their minds will be free from obstruction regarding all sentient beings, and they will swiftly realize unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment."
He further spoke this secret mantra:

"Hrīḥ. At that time, the World-Honored One, again relying upon all Tathāgatas, performed the rite of empowerment for the sake of all sentient beings, and for the sake of the bodhisattvas, he taught the Dharma-gate of the Principle of the Perfection of Wisdom (Prajñāpāramitā) for the empowerment of all sentient beings.
That is to say:
"All sentient beings are the Tathāgatagarbha, because the nature of Samantabhadra Bodhisattva is all-pervasive;
all sentient beings are vajras, because their nature is the perfection of empowerment."
All sentient beings are the nature of the treasury of the True Dharma, for they are able to turn the wheel of all the words of the True Dharma;
all sentient beings are the nature of the treasury of activities, for they are able to perform all activities in accordance with reality.
When the Buddha had thus spoken this Dharma of the profound principle for the empowerment of sentient beings, the supreme treasury, he addressed Vajrapāṇi Bodhisattva and the others, saying:

"If there are those who hear this Dharma gate of the supreme treasury of the all-pervading Prajñā-principle, and who believe, understand, uphold, recite, and correctly contemplate it with mindfulness, they shall be able to penetrate the dharmatā of the supreme treasury and swiftly realize unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment."
He further spoke these secret words:

"Ṭri. At that time, the World-Honored One, relying again upon the ultimate, exhaustive characteristic of all Tathāgatas—which is immeasurable, boundless, and without limit—proclaimed for the sake of the bodhisattvas the Dharma-gate of the Principle of the Prajñāpāramitā of the Equality of All Dharmas, which is immeasurable, boundless, and without limit, reaching the ultimate exhaustion.
That is to say:
"Because the profound *prajñāpāramitā* is immeasurable, all Tathāgatas are also immeasurable;
because the profound *prajñāpāramitā* is boundless, all Tathāgatas are also boundless."
Because the profound *prajñāpāramitā* is of a single nature, all phenomena are also of a single nature;
because the profound *prajñāpāramitā* is ultimately exhausted, all phenomena are also ultimately exhausted.
When the Buddha had thus spoken this Vajra of the Ultimate Principle that is Boundless and Limitless, he addressed the Bodhisattva Vajrapāṇi and the others, saying: “Vajrapāṇi!

If anyone hears this ultimate *prajñāpāramitā* method of the Vajra Dharma-gate, and with faith, understanding, and resolve, upholds, recites, and correctly contemplates it, all obstacles whatsoever shall be utterly extinguished without remainder; they will certainly attain the nature of the Tathāgata Vajradhara and swiftly realize unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment.
He further spoke these secret words:

“Vīrya. At that time, the World-Honored One, relying upon the Vairocana-aspect of the secret dharmatā free from conceptual proliferation of all Tathāgatas, proclaimed for the sake of all bodhisattvas the Great Bliss Vajra Amogha mantra of Samantabhadra—the Dharma-gate of the profound Prajñāpāramitā principle, which definitively enters the nature of all phenomena, is without beginning, middle, or end, and is the most supreme and foremost.
That is to say:
"Because all bodhisattvas are able to extensively perform services and offerings, they attain supreme great bliss;
because they are able to attain supreme great bliss, they are able to attain the unsurpassed great bodhi of all buddhas."
Because they have attained the unsurpassed Great Bodhi of all Buddhas, they are able to subdue all demonic armies;
because they have subdued all demonic armies, they attain the supreme accomplishment of mastery over the three realms;

because they have attained the supreme accomplishment of mastery over the three realms, they are able to universally benefit all sentient beings, bestowing upon them ultimate and most excellent peace and happiness.
He further spoke these secret words:
"There is one of supreme wisdom who, ever remaining within the cycle of birth and death,
extensively delivers all sentient beings, yet does not enter nirvana."
The Prajñāpāramitā is the ultimate wisdom of skillful means;
it can accomplish pure karma and universally purify all realms of existence.
Furthermore, by means of [the transformation of] greed and the like, it subdues all worlds.
Even reaching up to the Peak of Existence, The fruit is pure and unconditioned.
Abiding within the cycle of birth and death, Worldly dharmas cannot defile them;
Like the wondrous color of a lotus flower, They remain unstained by dust or grime.
"The person of great desire who is pure, the person who bestows great peace and happiness,
who possesses mastery over the three realms, performs steadfast benefit.
He then spoke these secret words:
"Hā! Oṃ namas sarvabuddhabodhisattvānām. Oṃ budhitiṣṭha vajre. Oṃ samantabhadra-carye. Oṃ jñānamani-tva. Oṃ gaṇi-ru-te-dha. Oṃ."

If one recites: *ĀṂ MAHĀRĀGADHYE* | *ĀṂ MERIYAKAVACE RĀJĀ* | *ĀṂ SARVAGAMINI* | *ĀṂ VAJRA NṚTYAKAVACE HŪṂ* | *ĀṂ SARVATATHĀGATAKOŚA* | *ĀṂ BĀVABĀVASHUDDHE PRABHA* | *ĀṂ DHARMATĀNANAVISHUDDHE DHVAJA* | *ĀṂ KARMAVISHUDANI OM HĀ* | *ĀṂ NISVABHAVAJRIṆI HŪṂ PHAṬ* | *ĀṂ KARMA LĀNILI* | *ĀṂ JAHU VAJRE IN* | *ĀṂ SARVANAYINI* | *ĀṂ DUNRIKA* | *ĀṂ AKĀROMUKHE HŪṂ*.

*Phrīṃ jvala pradyota hūṃ khaṃ vaṃ hūṃ kaṃ | Oṃ phaṭ amṛte | Oṃ sarvatathāgatamoghisiddhiye | Oṃ sarvatathāgatakāyavajra buddha | Oṃ sarvatathāgatacittavajra hṛdaya | Oṃ vajrasattva viśodhaya sarvapāpān mamāntike pramokṣaya sarvapāpāni niṣiddhe sarvasattvān sarvatathāgatasamayavajra hūṃ traṭ |* After the Buddha had spoken these secret words, he addressed the Bodhisattva Vajrapāṇi, the Lord of Secrets, saying:

"If any sentient beings hear this secret dharma-gate of the profound *prajñāpāramitā* method of the twenty-five [aspects], and with faith, understanding, and resolve, uphold, read, recite, and correctly contemplate it, they shall in this very life attain the supreme accomplishment of the vajra secrets of all Tathāgatas, and before long, they shall attain the body of the dharmatā of the Great Vajradhara of all Tathāgatas."
At that time, the World-Honored One, having proclaimed the aforementioned Dharma-gates to the bodhisattvas, further addressed the Bodhisattva Vajrapāṇi, saying: “Vajrapāṇi!”

This sutra of mine is difficult to hear; even if one hears as little as a single word, you should know that such a person has in the past already made offerings to various Buddhas and planted roots of goodness in the presence of those Buddhas.

How much more so for one who fully hears, receives, upholds, recites, and mindfully contemplates it; you should know that such a person has certainly already made offerings to, honored, revered, and praised eighty billion nayutas of Ganges-sands of Buddhas.
Wherever this sutra may be located, that place shall be as if it possessed a stupa of all Buddhas.
If there are sentient beings who cherish and revere this sutra, constantly following, guarding, and never parting from it, such persons should receive the respect and offerings of all the world;
such persons shall attain the supernormal power of recollecting past lives and be able to know the events of immeasurable kalpas in the past.
They shall not be disturbed or confused by any devas, Māras, or Pāpīyans; the Four Great Kings and all other devas will constantly follow and protect them;
they will be perpetually honored and sustained by all Buddhas and Bodhisattvas, and they will be reborn in the pure lands of the ten directions according to their vows.

Vajrapāṇi! I have now briefly explained the merits of this Dharma gate of the Prajñāpāramitā-naya in this manner; were it to be explained in detail, they would not be exhausted even at the end of an eon.

When the Buddha had finished speaking this sutra, Vajrapāṇi and the other bodhisattvas, as well as the entire assembly—including devas, nāgas, yakṣas, gandharvas, asuras, garuḍas, kiṃnaras, mahoragas, humans, and non-humans—all rejoiced greatly, and they faithfully accepted and practiced it.
The Vajraśekhara Yoga Prajñāpāramitā Sūtra on the Principles of Conduct (Tattvārthā-nāma-prajñāpāramitā-upadeśa-sūtra)
